vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-15308
vulnerability.description: cpython CPU-exhaustion DoS in html.parser.HTMLParser incremental feed() via repeated unterminated markup declarations (PSF-2026-33, CWE-407, High CVSS 7.5/8.7). Fix merged to the cpython 3.13 branch on 2026-07-04 (PR #153040) but as of 2026-07-13 no released CPython contains it — v3.13.14 (2026-06-10), v3.14.6, and v3.15.0b3 all predate the fix, so no base-image bump can remediate yet.

statements.impact_statement: The trigger requires incrementally feeding attacker-controlled HTML containing repeated unterminated markup declarations into html.parser.HTMLParser.feed(). aiperf 0.11.0 source contains zero references to html.parser, HTMLParser, or any html stdlib import (verified with `grep -rn -E 'html\.parser|HTMLParser|^(import|from) html'` against the aiperf 0.11.0 wheel — no hits). AICR invokes aiperf-bench exclusively as `aiperf profile <text-LLM> --url <endpoint>` (validators/performance/inference_perf_constraint.go); the workload exchanges only JSON over HTTP via aiohttp + msgspec/orjson and never parses HTML documents from the inference endpoint or any other source. No attacker-controlled markup can reach the vulnerable parser, so the quadratic-complexity code path is unreachable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2025-59375
vulnerability.description: libexpat before 2.7.2 allows attackers to trigger large dynamic memory allocations via a small document submitted for parsing (CVSS 3.1 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H). Present via Debian libexpat1 2.7.1-2 in the distroless runtime base; fixed in 2.8.2-1~deb13u1.

statements.impact_statement: Reaching the allocation amplification requires feeding a crafted XML document to expat's parser. The aiperf-bench runtime base moved to nvcr.io/nvidia/distroless/python:3.13-v4.0.8, which ships Debian libexpat1 2.7.1-2 (fixed upstream in 2.8.2-1~deb13u1). The package cannot be bumped from this repo: it comes from NVIDIA's published distroless image and 3.13-v4.0.8 is the newest 3.13 tag on nvcr.io, so no base-image bump remediates it today. Two independent facts make the vulnerable build unreachable. (1) Nothing in the image links it: reading ELF DT_NEEDED entries for every binary under /usr/local/lib, /usr/lib, /lib, /opt/venv/lib, /usr/local/bin, and /usr/bin returns zero references to libexpat, so /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libexpat.so.1 (2.7.1-2) is never loaded. (2) The one XML path that does execute does not use it: CPython routes xml.parsers.expat through lib-dynload/pyexpat.cpython-313-x86_64-linux-gnu.so, whose DT_NEEDED is ['libc.so.6'] only because expat is statically bundled at EXPAT_VERSION 2.8.1. So the 14 venv packages that import xml.* (PIL, matplotlib, pandas, fontTools, pyarrow, datasets, ...) exercise that bundled build, not the flagged 2.7.1-2 package. Whether 2.8.1 is itself patched varies by CVE and is stated per statement below. aiperf itself imports no XML module at all: scanning its 682 .py files for '^(import|from) (xml|pyexpat|xmlrpc)' returns zero hits. AICR invokes the image only as `aiperf profile <text-LLM> --url <endpoint>` (buildAIPerfJob in validators/performance/inference_perf_constraint.go), exchanging JSON over HTTP; no XML document from any source reaches a parser. The statically bundled expat is 2.8.1, above this CVE's 2.7.2 fix threshold, so even the reachable XML path is already patched.

vulnerability.name: GO-2026-5942
vulnerability.description: Parsing an invalid SVCB or HTTPS resource record can panic in golang.org/x/net/dns/dnsmessage (CVE-2026-46600, High). Present via golang.org/x/net v0.52.0 recorded in the Go build info of the embedded kyverno/chainsaw binary; fixed in golang.org/x/net v0.56.0. No bump remediates: chainsaw v0.2.15 (2026-05-06) is the latest upstream release and chainsaw's unreleased main branch is still on golang.org/x/net v0.53.0.

statements.impact_statement: The flagged package is golang.org/x/net v0.52.0, recorded in the Go build info of /usr/local/bin/chainsaw -- the upstream, cosign-attested kyverno/chainsaw binary copied into the image by cmd/gate/Dockerfile. grype reports the match location as /usr/local/bin/chainsaw, so the AICR gate binary is not implicated: /gate is built -mod=vendor -trimpath from this repo's go.mod, which pins golang.org/x/net v0.57.0 (already past the v0.56.0 fix), and `go version -m /gate` records zero dependency module versions, so grype cannot attribute any module finding to it. No bump remediates -- chainsaw v0.2.15 (2026-05-06) is the latest release and chainsaw's unreleased main is still on golang.org/x/net v0.53.0, below the v0.56.0 fix. The vulnerable code from the flagged module is not in the image. GO-2026-5942 is scoped to package golang.org/x/net/dns/dnsmessage (advisory symbols Message.Unpack, Parser.SVCBResource, Parser.HTTPSResource, unpackSVCBResource, and the Parser.All* accessors). Every dnsmessage function name in the chainsaw binary's pclntab carries the `vendor/` prefix -- `vendor/golang.org/x/net/dns/dnsmessage.*` -- which is the Go toolchain's own copy vendored inside the standard library's net package for the pure-Go resolver, not the golang.org/x/net module grype matched; grepping the binary for the unprefixed module path `golang.org/x/net/dns/dnsmessage` returns zero hits, so no code from the flagged module version is linked. The Go vulnerability database carries no `stdlib` entry aliased to CVE-2026-46600 (the index at https://vuln.go.dev/index/vulns.json returns only GO-2026-5942, scoped to the module), so the toolchain's vendored copy is not covered by this advisory; consistent with that, unpackSVCBResource -- the function the advisory names as panicking -- is absent from the vendored copy's surviving unpackers, which after dead-code elimination are only unpackA/AAAA/CNAME/MX/NS/PTR/SRV/TXT plus the primitive unpackBytes/Class/Text/Type/Uint helpers. Independently, chainsaw runs inside AICR only as an ephemeral, cluster-internal readiness-gate Job that `chainsaw test`s recipe-authored assertions against the trusted in-cluster Kubernetes API server (cmd/gate/Dockerfile, pkg/chainsawgate/runner); it never parses DNS wire-format messages from an attacker-controlled resolver.

vulnerability.description: Infinite loop on invalid input in golang.org/x/text: a norm.Iter can spin forever on input containing invalid UTF-8 bytes (CVE-2026-56852, High). Present via golang.org/x/text v0.35.0 recorded in the Go build info of the embedded kyverno/chainsaw binary; fixed in golang.org/x/text v0.39.0. No bump remediates: chainsaw v0.2.15 (2026-05-06) is the latest upstream release and chainsaw's unreleased main branch is still on golang.org/x/text v0.36.0.

statements.impact_statement: The flagged package is golang.org/x/text v0.35.0, recorded in the Go build info of /usr/local/bin/chainsaw -- the upstream, cosign-attested kyverno/chainsaw binary copied into the image by cmd/gate/Dockerfile. grype reports the match location as /usr/local/bin/chainsaw; the AICR gate binary is not implicated (this repo's go.mod pins golang.org/x/text v0.40.0, past the v0.39.0 fix, and `go version -m /gate` records no dependency module versions at all). No bump remediates -- chainsaw v0.2.15 (2026-05-06) is the latest release and chainsaw's unreleased main is still on golang.org/x/text v0.36.0, below v0.39.0. The defect itself is not in the image. Per the upstream report (go.dev/issue/80142, fix CL 794100, landed as golang/text commit 5ae8e578e495 'unicode/norm: avoid infinite loop on invalid input'), the hang lives in norm.Iter: nextComposed in unicode/norm/iter.go failed to advance when compInfo returned a zero-size Properties for an invalid UTF-8 byte; the fix makes compInfo return {flags: 0x80, size: 1} and adds Properties.isInvalid for normalize.go's patchTail. Enumerating every golang.org/x/text/unicode/norm function name in the chainsaw binary's pclntab that does NOT carry the standard library's `vendor/` prefix yields exactly five: compInfo, Form.Properties, Properties.Decomposition, Properties.combinesBackward, and init. Iter, nextComposed, patchTail, normReader.Read, and normWriter.Write are all absent -- the sole nextComposed anywhere in the binary is `vendor/golang.org/x/text/unicode/norm.nextComposed`, the Go 1.26.0 toolchain's own vendored copy reached through net/http's IDNA path, which is governed by the Go release cycle rather than the module version grype matched (the Go vulnerability database has no `stdlib` entry aliased to CVE-2026-56852). Disclosed for completeness: the advisory's symbol list does include Form.Properties, which IS linked here. That list is a conservative caller-closure over the patched compInfo -- it enumerates every exported entry point that can observe the corrected Properties -- but Form.Properties contains no loop; it returns the properties of a single rune. Reaching an unbounded loop requires an Iter (Iter.Init/Iter.InitString -> Iter.Next -> nextComposed) or patchTail to consume the zero-size Properties and fail to advance, and none of those are linked. Independently, chainsaw runs inside AICR only as an ephemeral, cluster-internal readiness-gate Job asserting recipe-authored conditions against the trusted in-cluster Kubernetes API server, so it never normalizes attacker-supplied text.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-11940
vulnerability.description: cpython: tarfile.extractall() under the 'data' or 'tar' filter can be bypassed by a crafted archive in which a hardlink references a symlink stored at a deeper name than the hardlink itself, letting the recreated symlink escape the destination directory (GHSA-9mc4-rqmq-h467, High; incomplete fix of CVE-2025-4330). Present via CPython 3.13.14 in the nvcr.io/nvidia/distroless/python:3.13-v4.0.8 runtime base. No bump remediates: 3.13.14 is the newest CPython 3.13 release, 3.13-v4.0.8 is the newest 3.13 tag on nvcr.io, grype's only known fixed version is 3.15.0b4 (an unreleased beta), and scanning the newest 3.14-line tag (3.14-v4.0.9, CPython 3.14.6) reports this same finding, so no minor-version move escapes it either.

statements.impact_statement: Triggering this requires extracting an attacker-supplied tar archive with tarfile.extractall(). aiperf 0.11.0 never touches tarfile: grepping the installed package at /opt/venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/aiperf for 'tarfile|extractall' returns zero hits. Across the entire venv (297 installed distributions) exactly one tar extraction exists -- datasets/utils/extract.py:130-131, TarExtractor.extract, which does `tarfile.open(input_path)` then `tar_file.extractall(output_path, members=TarExtractor.safemembers(tar_file, output_path))` -- inside the HuggingFace `datasets` package. aiperf declares that dependency (Requires-Dist: datasets>=3.0) but imports it from only two regions: the HuggingFace dataset loaders (aiperf/dataset/loader/base_hf_dataset.py, aiperf/dataset/loader/hf_asr.py) and the accuracy benchmark suites (aiperf/accuracy/benchmarks/{mmlu,gsm8k,aime,aime24,aime25,hellaswag,gpqa_diamond,math_500}.py). AICR reaches neither. buildAIPerfJob (validators/performance/inference_perf_constraint.go) launches the image with a fixed argv -- `aiperf profile --model <model> --url <endpoint> --endpoint-type chat --streaming --concurrency N --request-count N --warmup-request-count N --prompt-input-tokens-mean 128 --prompt-input-tokens-stddev 0 --prompt-output-tokens-mean 128 --prompt-output-tokens-stddev 0 --num-dataset-entries 100 --random-seed 100 --extra-inputs temperature:0 --output-artifact-dir /tmp/aiperf --export-level summary` -- with no --input-file, no public-dataset selector, and no accuracy flag. aiperf's dataset dispatch (aiperf/dataset/dataset_manager.py:444-456) therefore falls past the accuracy-enabled, PublicDataset, and FileDataset branches into _load_synthetic_dataset(), which generates prompts in-process from --random-seed and --num-dataset-entries. No archive is fetched and no tar is opened anywhere in the benchmark run. Note on the CVE's precondition: it describes a bypass of the 'data'/'tar' extraction filter, and that single call site passes no filter= argument at all (it screens members itself via safemembers), so the filter the CVE defeats is not the mechanism in use there -- but the operative reason this image is unaffected is that the call site is never executed by AICR's workload.
